Pescadero Harvest Blanket Knitting Pattern

Kristen McDonnell
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:56
Instaread

The Pescadero Harvest Blanket features a cozy checkerboard texture created with a simple combination of Seed, Stockinette, and Reverse Stockinette stitches.

This reversible blanket is knit in one piece with bulky-weight yarn and includes instructions for four sizes: Stroller, Baby, Lapghan, and Throw.

Pattern Instructions and Yarn Kit

PURCHASE PATTERN ONLY SHOP YARN KIT + PATTERN

The downloadable pattern is designed for knitters who enjoy clear, organized directions they can print or save digitally. It includes the stitch pattern, blanket measurements, yarn amounts, and finishing notes in one easy-to-follow printable pattern.

I also have a small batch of Pescadero Harvest Blanket Yarn Kits available for knitters who would like to create their blanket with my same yarn.

Each kit includes Cascade Superwash® 128 yarn for your selected blanket size. This bulky-weight yarn is soft, cozy, easy to care for, and beautifully smooth on your needles.

About This Pattern

The Pescadero Harvest Blanket is an easy knit and purl pattern with a cozy checkerboard texture. Smooth and bumpy stitch sections alternate to create a woven effect that looks beautiful on both sides.

This beginner-friendly blanket uses only knit and purl stitches, with no cables, increases, decreases, or special techniques. It is worked flat in one piece with bulky-weight yarn, making it a relaxing project that grows quickly.

Skill Level

This project is best suited for experienced beginning knitters who are comfortable knitting flat on a long circular needle and working simple slip stitches.

Included Sizes

The printable Pescadero Harvest Blanket pattern includes four blanket sizes:

  • Stroller Blanket: 20 x 25 in (51 x 64 cm)
  • Baby Blanket: 26 x 36 in (66 x 91 cm)
  • Lapghan: 39 x 47 in (99 x 119 cm)
  • Throw Blanket: 51 x 58 in (130 x 147 cm)

Blanket Construction

The Pescadero Harvest Blanket is knit flat in one piece. You will cast on your stitches, work the checkerboard texture across the blanket, then bind off and weave in your ends.

Reversible Stitch Texture

The Pescadero Harvest Blanket is an enlarged version of my recent Checkerboard Triple Weave Stitch, adapted into a cozy blanket design. Because the stitch pattern is reversible, both sides of the blanket look nearly identical.

This reversible texture uses a simple combination of four beginner-friendly stitch patterns:

  • Border in Garter Stitch
  • Blanket Body in Seed, Stockinette, and Reverse Stockinette Stitches

Together, these stitches create a checkerboard design with smooth and bumpy blocks. This larger blanket scale gives the texture a warm, woven look inspired by the harvest rows of Pescadero’s coastal farms.

Knitting Supplies

Bulky Weight #5 Yarn

To knit the Pescadero Harvest Blanket, you will need bulky-weight yarn and knitting needles that help you match the pattern gauge.

Favorite Yarn: The samples shown were knit with Cascade 128 Superwash Merino, a soft wool yarn that beautifully highlights the checkerboard texture.

Yarn Amounts:

  • Stroller: 301 yards (275 meters)
  • Baby: 596 yards (545 meters)
  • Lapghan: 1,132 yards (1,035 meters)
  • Throw: 1,893 yards (1,731 meters)

Tools

  • 1 Circular Knitting Needle #10 US / 6.0 mm, 36” length
  • Tapestry Needle
  • Scissors
  • Stitch Marker – I just use a little scrap of yarn with a slip knot
  • Blocking Mats & T-Pins (optional)

Knitting Techniques and Abbreviations

Need to brush up or learn a new technique? Check out my entire library of Knitting Techniques to help you along as you knit up this pattern.

  • BO = Bind Off
  • CO = Long Tail Cast On
  • K = Knit Stitch
  • P = Purl Stitch
  • PM = Place Marker
  • RM = Remove Marker
  • SL1 WYIF = Slip 1 St Purlwise with Yarn in Front
  • SM = Slip Marker
  • Sts = Stitches
  • Weave in Yarn Tails
  • * * = Repeat Pattern Between Asterisks

Local Inspiration in Pescadero, California

This blanket is named for Pescadero, a favorite local coastal farming town along California Highway 1, south of my knitting studio. The area’s produce fields, tucked between the Pacific Ocean and rolling hills, grow coastal favorites like artichokes, strawberries, and pumpkins. Those tidy harvest rows inspired this blanket’s warm, woven design.
